scope: complete Host candidate retention with bounded continuation
Web filtered DOM observation and pagination
offline ownership archive browsing, query and explicit deletion
Android SDK original completion query without cancellation

nodeFunctional.note: Full suite before adding two final edge-case tests; no product source changed after this run began.

checks.name: native value setter dispatches actual browser input
contenteditable browser insertion reaches the editor
duplicate visible text does not dispatch
6000-control page keeps an observed element actionable after a label update
combined text, role and CSS select the intended Agree control
duplicate candidates beyond the first 20 can be queried, paged and selected
replacement with the same selector rejects old identity
returning to the same URL rejects an old page observation
focus replacement cannot write to the new input
an overlay prevents clicking the covered target
explicit scrolling makes the observed off-screen target reachable
Enter delivers one keydown even when the handler navigates

responseReplay.note: Same complete archived bodies and complete conversation bodies as the earlier audit, not new independent population samples. No original device action replayed.

localOwnershipArchiveSizes.note: Current default Host directory only; no historical private payload copied into the repo.

limits: No physical Android, OEM permission, native WebView or iPhone acceptance in this batch. Android completion-query verification is JVM plus controlled HTTP/ADB protocol evidence.
Web pagination is a fresh DOM observation; positions may shift. The chosen element remains bound to its actual ID and page.
SDK completion query uses existing retained original coordinator completion, not unlimited SDK receipt history. Missing or changed original runtime remains unknown.
Old corrupt force-stop files without serial metadata or a current-journal attribution are not silently assigned to a device.
Offline archive reads can be extracted directly but do not invent a persisted response reference. Large unparsed bytes retain an explicit filesystem path and deletion path.
Unified diagnosis, test workflow/preparation recipes and remaining selection/evidence-sampling assessments are still open.
